body: Craftsman houses are built to show off layered trim: corner boards, window casings, porch beams, and brackets. A single wall color with white trim can flatten all of that. Our color consultation in High Springs, FL often starts by deciding which details to highlight. That usually means a body color, a trim color, and sometimes a third color for doors, sashes, or porch ceilings, all based on the roof and any brick or stone.
If you're drawn to period-appropriate colors, our article on historic paint colors covers palettes that suit older North Central Florida homes.

Deep porches and mature trees mean many High Springs living rooms get soft, filtered light. Colors that look clean in a bright showroom can look gray or muddy here. Newer homes in Bridlewood and Bailey Estates often have the opposite problem, with large windows that wash out pale colors. That's why we paint full-size drawdowns on your actual walls and look at them in the morning and late afternoon. Our article on Florida interior paint colors gives you some starting points.

Sheen changes color too. The same color reads lighter in satin than in matte, and enamel trim catches light differently than a flat wall. We show sheens side by side on the drawdowns so the final result isn't a surprise.

faqs.q: How many colors should a craftsman house have?
faqs.a: Often three: a body color, a trim color, and an accent for doors, sashes, or porch details. Some homes look best with two. We test the combination with large samples before you decide.

faqs.q: Why do colors look darker in my older house?
faqs.a: Deep porches and tree cover reduce the light coming into the room, so colors look darker and grayer. Testing large samples in your actual rooms solves that.

faqs.q: Do you help downtown businesses choose storefront colors?
faqs.a: Yes. We look at the signage, awnings, and neighboring facades, then test a body and trim combination with large samples so the storefront fits the block and still gets noticed from the sidewalk.

faqs.q: Can you match the original color on my trim?
faqs.a: Yes. We can match from a chip, a leftover can, or a sample of the existing paint, then paint a drawdown so you can confirm the match.
